Before this change a timed-out retry saved its partial to the target.

When a write replaces a file holding a usage line, sum the earlier usage into the new KERYX_USAGE line so retried dispatches add up. problem: namedBySession re-scans the full text of every retained command for every stale open package, on every stop. The tracker keeps whole tool-call argument strings (up to 64) and only the count is capped, not their size.
impact: Failure mode: per-stop CPU stall in the keryx shell. A session that ran 64 `keryx review ingest`-style commands with inline reports of ~1 MB, in a checkout carrying ~50 stale open drafts (the case the comment names), does 50 x 2 ids x 64 x 1 MB, about 6 GB of indexOf scanning per model stop, on the event loop, plus the memory for the retained strings. Realistic argument sizes (KBs) make it negligible, so this is a bound that is missing, not a measured stall.
suggested_fix: When the tracker scans a call, extract only the review-id tokens it names (SAFE_REVIEW_ID-shaped words next to `keryx review`) into a capped Set and test membership; or truncate the stored arguments to a few KB. Then namedBySession is O(ids).

problem: The light-round recheck now runs git through defaultGitRunner, which spawns with no timeout and no kill signal, unlike gitTopLevel and gitDiffAt (15 s, SIGKILL). The result goes through processCache, which stores the pending promise and removes it only after it settles.
impact: Failure mode: if one `git merge-base` hangs (stalled network or FUSE file system, wedged git), the promise never settles and stays cached under that key. Every later readiness, complete and panel refresh in the same process awaits the same hung promise, so the gate and panel freeze until the process restarts. The other git calls in this path would fail after 15 s and be retried.
suggested_fix: Give defaultGitRunner (or the resolveBase call here) the same timeout and killSignal as gitDiffAt, and have processCache drop an entry that has not settled after a deadline.
evidence: coverage.ts spawns gitTopLevel/gitDiffAt with `timeout: 15_000, killSignal: "SIGKILL"`; prior-round.ts defaultGitRunner spawns with `stdout: "pipe", stderr: "ignore"` only.

problem: Only successful diff results are remembered. The case this flow targets, a merged PR with an empty range or no resolvable base, is an error result, so it is recomputed (rev-parse, up to five merge-base, and the diff) on each call.
impact: Failure mode: a light dispatch whose base cannot resolve costs about 7 git spawns per completion-gate evaluation and per panel refresh, at every model stop. That is wasted work, not an outage. A short negative TTL (a few seconds) would settle whether it matters; no load is stated.
suggested_fix: Remember errors for a short TTL, or key them by head and invalidate on a manifest mtime change.
evidence: processCache deletes the key when `keep(value)` is false.

problem: The cache key is package, root and the manifest target (kind, ref, recorded base, head). The base that is actually diffed is resolved later from origin/main or main and is not in the key.
impact: Observation: in a long-lived shell or panel process a cached success is served after the base ref moves, for example once the PR merges and `resolveBase` would now give an empty range. The light/full decision could then differ between a fresh process and the running one. Settled by checking whether the shell process outlives a fetch of the base branch.
suggested_fix: Include the resolved merge-base sha in the key, or cache only the diff after resolveBase has run.

The doc comment above packageDiffStats says an empty range 'is not a small diff: it refuses', but that only holds on the PR/base path.

For kind `branch`, resolve the base the way the PR path does (recorded base, else origin/main, main, ...) and diff against it, not against the ref. Run emptyRangeWarning on every resolved base, and refuse (full set) when it fires. Only `path`/`issue`/`report` refs, which are not revisions, should fall through to the existing git-failure refusal.

problem: Context.coverageGated says a closed package's recorded state is final and publish, the publish guard and the panel must not suddenly call it NOT READY. The flag is true for every package whose coverage.md carries COVERAGE_MD_MARK, which includes every package closed after flow 460. So for those closed packages reviewersCheck still runs packageCoverageErrors. For a light dispatch, that call re-derives the depth from live state: coverage.ts effectiveDepth runs packageDiffStats, which does a git diff of base...head at the repository top level, and then decideRoundDepth against the current project config. If the diff cannot be resolved, the depth falls back to full ('if ("error" in stats) return { depth: "full", refused: stats.error }'), and the full reviewer set then refuses the light dispatch.
impact: Trigger: a light-round PR package that closed READY after flow 460 is read again (readiness, the publish guard, the panel) in a checkout without the PR head commit, such as a fresh clone after a squash merge and branch delete. A later change to the depth thresholds or the risk-class config triggers it too. Outcome: item 3 fails with 'coverage gate (as review complete runs it): ... the diff could not be resolved', and a closed review flips to NOT READY. This is the same flip the flag was added to prevent, and the repair it names (dispatch the missing reviewers) cannot apply to a closed round.
suggested_fix: On a closed package, do not re-derive the depth from live git or config. Gate packageCoverageErrors on manifest.status !== 'closed' (open packages only), or have the closed path read the depth decision recorded at close (round-depth.json or the dispatch's own depth) instead of rechecking it. Keep the COVERAGE_MD_MARK test only for the item-6 omitted-reviewer check, which reads files and not live state.

problem: partitionRegionsByFix splits a region that holds both fix and new lines, and the context between the two kinds is shared half and half. On the split side, each piece therefore has fewer context lines than the configured window. Each piece still copies the parent's contextTruncated. If the parent window was complete, every piece says false.
impact: ScopedRegion documents contextTruncated as the signal that a window is narrower than asked, so a reviewer does not assume it saw the enclosing code. A fix or new piece cut from a mixed region claims a full window while it can hold as little as one context line on the cut side. The reviewer of the piece loses that warning. No wrong routing results: the cost is to the reader of the slice.

title: A re-dispatch to the same save_result_to overwrites the earlier dispatch's KERYX_USAGE line, so the empty dispatch's spend is lost and the total can read as complete
problem: Flow 460 (H) records an empty or timed-out child's usage by writing the placeholder plus a KERYX_USAGE line into save_result_to, because the dispatch was paid for. The empty-reply advice then tells the parent to re-dispatch once. Drivers fix one result path per reviewer x wave (raw/<reviewer>-w<n>.txt), so the re-dispatch saves to the same file. On a completed re-dispatch, saveChildResult overwrites the file, which removes the first dispatch's usage line. On a re-dispatch that times out or ends empty, saveTimedOutPartial sees a non-empty file and writes to `<target>.partial`, which readRaws (review-ledger.ts, `*.txt` only) never reads, so the second dispatch's usage is lost. In both cases the ledger counts one dispatch per raw file. usageTotals then reports `complete: true` / `token spend: X over N dispatch(es)` with no 'at least' qualifier, even though one paid dispatch is missing.
impact: The round's stated spend is silently understated on the exact path the PR added the empty-dispatch recording for (empty child, then the re-dispatch the advice prescribes). Acceptance criterion H ('every dispatch's token use lands in the package') does not hold there, and the report presents the figure as complete.
suggested_fix: Carry earlier usage forward rather than replacing it. When save_result_to already holds a KERYX_USAGE line, keep it: either append the new dispatch's line (splitUsage would need to sum lines, or the ledger would need to count each line as a dispatch), or write the superseded attempt's usage to a sidecar the ledger reads (for example raw/<name>.usage.jsonl), and fold it into usageTotals as its own dispatch. Add a test that runs an empty dispatch and then a completed one to the same path and asserts two dispatches and the summed tokens.

suggested_fix: Record the coverage gate's verdict at complete (for example in research.json or the manifest), then have readiness on a closed package read that record and not re-run git. Or treat an UNRESOLVED diff on a closed package as a note, not a failure.

title: An older open package counts as named by this session when attacker-controlled text matches a token of any keryx review command
problem: namedBySession treats a package as continued by this session when its manifest.reviewId or directory name appears as a token anywhere in the arguments of any `keryx review` tool call (completion-gate.ts:217). scanRoot passes the manifest's own reviewId at :252, and that value is attacker-controlled when the package is committed in the checked-out PR. A package whose reviewId is `keryx` or `review` is therefore named by every `keryx review` command. Separately, the tracker trusts `# managed review:` and `path:` lines in the result of any tool call whose arguments merely contain `keryx review` (:160, :165-172). With a compound command such as `keryx review status x; cat notes.md`, file content can name review ids and package dirs inside cwd.
attack_vector: The author of the PR under review commits `.metaproject/reviews/anything/manifest.json` with mode review-flow, status draft and reviewId "keryx". Take a session that resumes an earlier review without an active pointer, or one that has not opened its own package yet. Every `keryx review ...` call names that package, and it passes the stale-manifest filter at :252. pickPackage picks it as the newest candidate when its checkout mtime is later than the real package's manifest. The harness nudge then names the attacker's package and repeats its completion blockers to the model as harness-provenance text.

suggested_fix: Match a review id only against reviewIds keryx printed and against an explicit argument position (`review status|readiness|complete <id>`, `--review-id <id>`), not against any token of the command line; or ignore ids that equal a word of the command itself. Trust `path:`/`# managed review:` lines only when the tool call is a single `keryx review start|attach|ingest` command, not a compound shell line.
evidence: src/review/completion-gate.ts:202-208 namesToken matches any boundary-delimited token; :217 applies it to every recorded command; :252 passes manifest.reviewId from the package on disk; :160 accepts any call whose arguments contain `keryx review`. Test completion-gate.test.ts:245-246 covers only a call that is not a keryx review command.

title: A closed review-flow manifest committed by the reviewed PR under cwd still releases the completion gate

problem: Flow 460 L6 drops the union of a fix slice's roster with its round-1 content routing (458 M2/M3: 'a fix touching process spawning still gets the security reviewer'). In the next delta round those hunks are FIX hunks; the slice is routed to review-logic/review-regression/the LG author only; review-security-code never reads the new process-spawning code and keryx review routing/readiness reports nothing missing. A command-injection or path-traversal sink can merge with the security reviewer silently skipped. Alternatively, make commit-named marking in splitDelta only mark hunks that also overlap the named finding's file, so unrelated new code stays NEW.

[])])]`); src/review/routing-check.ts:37 `backedFix ? expectedFixRoles(entry, fix!, text) : needed.roles` (was union with needed.roles); src/review/prior-round.ts:738-749 commit-named loop marks every hunk of parseDiffHunks(own.stdout) across all files; src/review/slice-routing.ts:116-117 content rules route exec/spawn/child_process to review-security-code.

problem: isSecurityFinding decides whether review-security-code joins a fix slice from the prior finding's reviewer, a SEC id, or a keyword regex over its problem text. problem: In keryx shell the harness appends its KERYX_USAGE line only when the provider reported usage (`childUsage.known`). No gate reads usage, so this is the integrity of a reported figure only.
suggested_fix: Save `splitUsage(raw).body` (and the stripped partial text in the timeout path) before appending the harness's own line, so in keryx shell only the harness can state usage and an unreported dispatch stays unknown.

problem: screenedAs closes a raw finding `out-of-scope` when ANY screened entry has the same reviewer and the same bare display id (`entry.reviewer === reviewer && entry.id === fid`). Display ids are per-reply, not per-reviewer: every wave restarts at F-001 (round 1 of this PR alone has review-logic-w3:F-001 and review-logic-w4:F-001, both major). The obligation id `oid` (`<raw stem>:<fid>`) is wave-specific, but the fallback match ignores the raw file. So when the consolidated report uses bare ids (the schema and DISPLAY_ID_FORM allow it), and wave 1's F-001 was screened by the scope-B floor while wave 3's different F-001 was never put into findings.json, wave 3's obligation is closed `out-of-scope` with wave 1's screen reason and evidence `research-evidence/ingest-screened.json`. That file never screened that finding.

Outcome: `ledger build` reports rawReconciled with no gap, and the dropped finding (possibly a major or blocker) passes `review complete` unreported. The ledger obligations exist to catch exactly this. A record also points at a screen decision that was never made about this finding. The attacker here is the orchestrating agent, which the gate treats as untrusted: it can lose a finding with no disposition row, so nothing is left for the operator to see.
suggested_fix: Match a screened entry to the raw dispatch it came from, never to the reviewer alone. Have ingest record the obligation id or the raw source on each IngestScreened entry (the canonical id in stem form is already `oid`), and match only `entry.id === oid || entry.global_id === <global id of this raw finding>`. If the bare-id fallback has to stay, use it only when exactly one raw file of that reviewer carries `fid`. When several raw files do, leave the obligation unresolved and let a disposition close it.

A quote of one token (`x`, `)`, `return`), or of whitespace around one token, becomes a `derived` anchor whenever it occurs on exactly one line, and findings.json records it as method `substring`. The locator's stated purpose (module header: a report is attacker-influenced data, and a wrong anchor is worse than an honest `unlocatable`) is weakened. A fabricated or careless finding now gets a derived line from a fragment that proves the reviewer read nothing.

suggested_fix: Give the substring pass a floor, for example a minimum trimmed length (around 12 characters) or at least one identifier-like token plus one other character. Below the floor, return `unlocatable` with kind `absent` and a reason that says the quote is too short to anchor.

suggested_fix: Recognise a call as a keryx review command only when the command itself starts with `keryx review` (after an optional `cd … &&`), not when the words appear anywhere in the arguments.
